w: Swamishri left Vidyanagar at 6.15 p.m. Swamishri then left for Bochasan, arriving at the mandir at 7.53 p.m.

At 10.30 a.m., Pujya Viveksagar Swami spoke on the occasion of Kishore Day. The kishores performed a traditional dance and a seminar was presented by kishores of Tajpur on "The Necessity of Mandirs." Thereafter the kishores of Botad performed a drama on 'Vajesinh Darbar's Hookah.' Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.
Living with Swamishri
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of the canvas murtis of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Shri Radha Krishna Dev for a BAPS kutir mandir in Cheri village of Valsad district.
At 9.45 a.m. Swamishri gave diskha to 57 youths, out of which 18 youths were given parshad diksha and 39 parshads were given the bhagwati diksha.

At 6.30 p.m., the Shri Hari Jayanti celebration commenced with dhun and prayers. Thereafter Brahmadarshan Swami spoke about the purpose of Bhagwan Swaminarayan's birth. The story of Joban Pagi's transformation was enacted. Atmatrupt Swami spoke about the socio-spiritual activities performed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. A drama on Devji Bhagat's faith in Shriji Maharaj was performed. BAPS youths of Vadodara performed a beautiful traditional folk dance. Ishwarcharan Swami elaborated upon the divine nature of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. This was followed by another drama 'Bhaktavtsal Shri Hari' by youths. A speech on the impact of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Parampara was delivered by Viveksagar Swami. Thereafter the senior sadhus honored Swamishri with a variety of garlands. A traditional dance "Chaitra sud navami avi..." was performed by BAPS youths of Nadiad. In conclusion Swamishri blessed the assembly, "Bhagwan Swaminarayan came on this earth to redeem countless people. Today it is also the birth of Bhagwan Shri Ram. We have been blessed with the two celebrations so that we may attain Ram Rajya and Akshardham. We need Ram Rajya in our country. If we attain Ram Rajya, that is, the way in which Ram ruled our country, then there will be peace in India. And if we worship Bhagwan Swaminarayan then we will attain Akshardham and therefore eternal happiness... Bhagwan Swaminarayan gifted the Shikshapatri for the benefit of all mankind, regardless of distinction of color or religion." At 10.20 p.m. Swamishri performed the Shri Hari Jayanti celebration arti and then rocked Shri Harikrishna Maharaj in a decorated swing.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
28 March 2004, Nadiad

BAPS youths of Nadiad performed a total of 178,512 rosaries, 54,102 prostrations, 165,211 circumambulations and 84 waterless fasts for Swamishri's good health. They had started these austerities from 1 December 2003. Similarly devotees of Nadiad had performed a total 1,492,469 rosaries, 154,795 prostrations, 165,886 circumambulations, 138 waterless fasts and inspired 110 aspirants into Satsang assembly.
Today being Sunday, after his morning puja Pramukh Swami Maharaj himself expressed a wish to give blessings.

Swamishri said, "Today the Sunday assembly will be held here, because it is the command of Jogi Maharaj. The devotees of Botad come here specially to gain this benefit. Everyone is enthusiastic and joyful; they even come on foot. There is an understanding of glory, so devotion happens.

"Vyasji was very capable; he composed seventeen Puranas. The Varaha Purana, Kurma Purana, Narasimha Purana, Devi Purana: he wrote all these Puranas, yet he did not find peace. Then Vyasji told Naradji about his lack of peace. Then Naradji spoke of making firm the upasana of the manifest form of God.

"Worship of the atma and Paramatma, knowledge of the nature of the atma and Paramatma: that is true happiness. If the true form of God, the true form of the Sant and the true form of Brahman are rightly recognised, there is peace. But Vyasji spoke of all this indirectly. He did not sing the glory of the manifest God through whom liberation is attained; that is why he had no peace.

"Peace lies only in singing and listening to the divine episodes of God and God's devotees. We are to speak only His discourses, His kirtans, His talks. Just as Bhagatji understood the glory of Gunatitanand Swami, that 'This one seated is Akshar, this one lying down is Akshar', so he was filled with joy. The Bhakta Chintamani, Harililamrut and Satsangijivan contain the divine episodes of God and His devotees; if you read them, there will be peace.

"But even after attaining God, and a Sant like God, why is there no peace? The reason is attachment to the five kinds of sense objects. As long as there is attachment to eating and drinking, pleasures, bungalows and so on, however much is said, it does not sink in. If people sit here while discourses go on, but other thoughts are going on inside, how can there be peace!

"Not living according to the commands causes lack of peace. But if we live according to the commands, there is happiness and peace in every way. If you enjoy the five sense objects in relation to God, there is happiness, and if you enjoy them in relation to the world, there is misery. With the eyes have darshan of God, with the ears listen to God's discourses, and there will be peace. Let us pray to Maharaj that everyone receives such knowledge, such understanding, such happiness. We have received the happiness of God and the Sant; Shastriji Maharaj has given the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam. My blessings are that it becomes firm in our lives and that we become happy in it."

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj went up into the mandir for darshan of Thakorji, he must have seen Ghanshyambhai, originally from Bhaili and now living in Secunderabad. After that Swamishri did his puja, and after the puja Swamishri returned to his residence. Before the meal was brought, Swamishri called a sadhu and said, "That man from Bhaili has come, hasn't he! If he is leaving, give him prasad."
All his life Swamishri has looked after the devotees. The thread of his glance keeps the devotees' hearts bound to him.
During the meal, Gnananand Swami sang Sanskrit shlokas he had composed himself. While singing he said, "My tune is not good, but I am singing anyway."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "The feeling is good, isn't it!"
In "Sakhi! Uparna range rache nahi..." (Friend! He is not pleased by outward colour...), Nishkulanand Swami has described Shri Hari's natural disposition. The same is seen in Swamishri too.

In the course of a conversation today, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Earlier, we could manage to reach everywhere. As long as the body was well, we never said no to anyone. If we set out and two villages came on the way, we would cover those too, because in those days the body was good, the hands and feet worked and health was good too, and when we travelled, the devotees were pleased. Now we meet people once in the morning and then work sitting indoors all day. Once we go in, we stay in, and only come out again the next morning."

All his life Swamishri travelled from village to village for the uplift of the devotees and for the service of people. Now, because of his age and health and at the doctors' insistence, his travelling has reduced, yet his enthusiasm is still just as fresh!
When the talk turned to the walking pilgrimages and austerities of devotees, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Many people come walking."
Narayancharan Swami said, "There is only one reason, that your health stays good."
Yogicharan Swami said with a smile, "Everyone has sponsored your health."
Swamishri said, "That is fine, but if they walk from so far away, they will get tired, won't they!"
A sadhu said, "Just now a young man came walking alone from Surat."

Hearing this, Swamishri turned his hand in a gesture of wonder and admiration and said, "Walking pilgrimages have been going on since Maharaj's time. In the past too, groups of pilgrims used to come."
In this way Swamishri accepted the devotees' feelings.

Mahant Swami Maharaj's breakfast was nearly over. All the sadhus went to Ishwarcharandas Swami to receive sheera (a sweet semolina dish) as prasad (sanctified food). Swamishri beckoned Kamalnayandas Swami, who was standing nearby, and quietly said something to him. Kamalnayandas Swami joined the line as before, received the sheera prasad and went straight to Swamishri. Swamishri took a little of the prasad given by Ishwarcharandas Swami. Only then did everyone realize that Swamishri had asked Kamalnayandas Swami to bring the prasad given by Ishwarcharandas Swami's hand.
With a smile Swamishri said: "He wouldn't just give it to me like that."
How great is the glory of the sadhus in Swamishri's heart!

Today at breakfast the talk was about the virtues of the sadhus. Later, as he went to rest, Mahant Swami Maharaj said: "Now I won't be able to sleep. There has been a pumping of mahima (glory), hasn't there!"

A letter had come from a woman in America. Ever since Pramukh Swami Maharaj had gone to Akshardham (the divine abode of God), she had felt very restless and deeply sad at heart. One night she had a dream. Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj were standing before the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj in the Vartal mandir. Then both gurus merged into the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj. A few days later she had another dream, in which Pramukh Swami Maharaj told her firmly: "You will have to love Mahant Swami just as you love me. There is no other way."

After hearing these words, she became so attached to Swamishri that she stopped remembering Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Because of this she became very troubled, and she asked Swamishri: "What should I do?"
Swamishri sent word: "We must remember Bapa. Even if nothing else is remembered, at least remember this much: Pramukh Swami Maharaj is the guru of Mahant Swami Maharaj."
The woman had further asked: "Are you and Pramukh Swami Maharaj one and the same?"
Swamishri said: "Both are one. That is why they merged into God."

Swamishri was referring to the dream she herself had described, in which both gurus had merged into the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj. These answers Swamishri gave were the kind that turn the doubts of many into clarity.
During the evening walk, the reading of the book "Digantma Danka" began. In it came the passage: "On seeing Yogibapa, the African brothers would say, 'Iko Mungu... Iko Mungu...'"
Mahant Swami Maharaj asked what it meant. The sadhus said: "It means 'This is God... This is God...'"

Speaking of how the same experience comes even today through Swamishri's darshan, Yogimanandas Swami said: "A local African brother serves as a worker on the lowest floor. You blessed him today, and he is filled with joy. He says: 'God himself has blessed me. If I had been anywhere else, I would not have received such a blessing. He has given me strength through his blessings.'"
"The Sant is Hari himself": seekers here too have this experience.

While taking his meal, Mahant Swami Maharaj noticed that Mahendrakaka's feet were touching the bare floor. Thinking, "He must be feeling cold," he gestured to Priyavratdas Swami and made him understand that something should be placed beneath them. At once a mat was placed under Mahendrakaka's feet. Swamishri was pleased.
What care he has for elderly devotees!
